# Star a GitHub Repository with Composio CLI

## Background

Composio provides a CLI to interact with over 1000+ toolkits. You can execute tools directly from your terminal. In this task, you will use the Composio CLI to star a specific GitHub repository.

## Requirements

* Use the Composio CLI to star the repository `composiohq/composio`.
* The operation must be performed on behalf of the user `zealt-user01`.

## Implementation Guide

1. Ensure you are logged in to Composio (the `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` is already set in your environment).
2. Use the `composio execute` command to call the GitHub star tool.
3. The tool slug for starring a repository is `GITHUB_STAR_A_REPOSITORY_FOR_THE_AUTHENTICATED_USER`.
4. Provide the required arguments: `owner` as `composiohq` and `repo` as `composio`.

## Constraints

* Project path: /home/user/star-task
* Use Composio CLI.
* User ID: `zealt-user01`

## Integrations

* Composio
* GitHub

Try [1mexecute[22m sooner than you'd think — it validates inputs, checks connections, and tells
you what to fix.

Use [1mdev[22m when you are building an agent with Composio's SDK and want scaffolding,

[1mUSAGE[22m
  composio <command> [options]

[1mMODE[22m
  default help

[1mCORE COMMANDS[22m
  [1msearch[22m
    Find tools by use case across all toolkits/apps.
    [2mUsage:[22m composio search <query...> [--toolkits text] [--limit integer] [--human]
      [2m<query...>          [22mOne or more semantic use-case queries (e.g. "send emails" "github issues")
      [2m--toolkits          [22mFilter by toolkit slugs, comma-separated
      [2m--limit             [22mMaximum number of results (1-1000)
      [2m--human             [22mShow formatted output instead of default JSON

  [1mexecute[22m
    Execute a tool. Validates inputs and connections automatically; use it aggressively.
    [2mUsage:[22m composio execute <slug> [-d, --data text] [--file path] [--dry-run] [--get-schema] | execute -p <slug> -d <text> <slug> -d <text> ...
      [2m<slug>              [22mTool slug (e.g. "GITHUB_CREATE_ISSUE")
      [2m-d, --data          [22mJSON or JS-style object arguments, e.g. -d '{ repo: "foo" }', @file, or - for stdin
      [2m-p, --parallel      [22mExecute repeated <slug> -d <text> pairs concurrently
      [2m--file              [22mInject a local file path into the single file_uploadable input
      [2m--dry-run           [22mValidate and preview the tool call without executing it
      [2m--get-schema        [22mFetch and print the CLI-facing input schema

  [1mlink[22m
    Connect your account for a toolkit/app.
    [2mUsage:[22m composio link [<toolkit>]
      [2m<toolkit>           [22mToolkit slug to link (e.g. "github", "gmail")

  [1mrun[22m
    Run inline TS/JS code with shimmed CLI commands; injected execute(), search(), proxy(), experimental_subAgent(), and z (zod).
    [2mUsage:[22m composio run <code> [-- ...args] | run [-f, --file text] [-- ...args] [--dry-run]
      [2m<code>              [22mInline Bun ESNext code to evaluate
      [2m-f, --file          [22mRun a TS/JS file instead of inline code
      [2m--dry-run           [22mPreview execute() calls without running remote actions

  [1mproxy[22m
    curl-like access to any toolkit API through Composio using your connected account.
    [2mUsage:[22m composio proxy <url> --toolkit text [-X method] [-H header]... [-d data]
      [2m<url>               [22mFull API endpoint URL
      [2m--toolkit           [22mToolkit slug whose connected account should be used
      [2m-X, --method        [22mHTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH)
      [2m-H, --header        [22mHeader in "Name: value" format. Repeat for multiple.
      [2m-d, --data          [22mRequest body as raw text, JSON, @file, or - for stdin

[90m  Typical flow: search → execute (link and tools when needed)[39m

[1mTOOLS[22m
  composio tools info <slug>        Print tool summary and cache its schema
  composio tools list <toolkit>     List tools available in a toolkit
  composio triggers info <slug>     Print trigger type details and schema summaries
  composio triggers list <toolkit>  List available trigger types in a toolkit
  composio artifacts cwd            Print the cwd-scoped session artifact directory


[1mEXAMPLES[22m
